name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: The close-grip lat pulldown uses a V-bar or narrow handle attachment that positions the elbows close to the torso during the pull. This grip allows a greater range of elbow travel and places substantial load on the biceps alongside the lats, making it a preferred variation for lifters seeking combined lat and biceps development or for those transitioning toward chin-up proficiency.

execution.starting_position: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and attach a V-bar or close-grip handle. Adjust the thigh pad to secure the legs. Grasp the handle with a neutral grip and extend the arms fully overhead, allowing the lats to stretch.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a V-bar or close-grip handle to the lat pulldown machine pulley. Set an appropriate weight. Secure thighs under the pad.
steps: Step 1: Begin seated with arms fully extended overhead, lats on stretch.
Step 2: Depress the shoulder blades and initiate the pull by driving the elbows down toward the hips.
Step 3: Pull the bar toward the upper chest, bringing the elbows close to the sides of the torso.
Step 4: At the bottom, squeeze the lats and hold briefly.
Step 5: Return slowly to full arm extension, maintaining scapular control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull the bar down. Inhale as you return to the starting position.
common_mistakes: Leaning back excessively, which turns the movement into a partial row
Pulling the bar behind the head, which stresses the cervical spine
Using momentum by rocking the torso
safety_considerations: Never pull behind the head — always pull to the front of the chest
Maintain a neutral or slightly arched lumbar spine throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the top to the bar reaching the upper chest at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Think 'elbows to ribs' and they will naturally come to the right position
Let your chest rise slightly to meet the bar at the bottom
